newsitem.title: CANADA: Midland Walwyn shares jump on rumors.
newsitem.headline: Midland Walwyn shares jump on rumors.

text.p: Shares in Midland Walwyn Inc jumped on Friday as rumors swirled that Bank of Nova Scotia's ScotiaMcLeod Inc may be on the brink of taking over the last large independent broker in Canada.
The stock jumped to a 52-week high of 12.00 in brisk dealings before pulling back midafternoon to trade 1.20 higher at 11.85.

"There's a rumor that ScotiaMcLeod is going to take out Midland this weekend," said one trader who asked not to be identified. Another dealer said the price the rumor mill was kicking around was C$11 per share cash.
Another rumor pegged the price as high as C$18 a share.
Peter Kahnert, a spokesman for Midland Walwyn, said the market rumors are false.
"Those are just rumors." Kahnert said, adding that the brokerage firm has not had talks with ScotiaMcLeod or any other potential suitor.
ScotiaMcleod spokesperson Donna Cox also denied the speculation as "purely rumors."
ScotiaMcLeod senior vice-president Fred Ketchen said that he had heard the rumors, but put them down to idle chatter caused by a lull in market action.
"The rumors that started when DS (RBC Dominion Securities Inc) took over Richardson Greenshields were that Midland would be the next to go," Ketchen said.

Traders said ScotiaMcLeod would be considered a logical choice because it has not made a major purchase in a number of years, despite the acquisition of Burns Fry by Nesbitt Thomson and of Richardson Greenshields by RBC Dominion Securities, a unit of Royal Bank of Canada.
"If such a thing is in the works, I certainly don't know about it," Ketchen said.
